https://www.politico.eu/article/nigel-fa.text: BIRMINGHAM, England — Britain’s Nigel Farage plans to visit France by the end of October to meet Marine Le Pen, the president of the far-right National Rally (RN), according to an official with the Reform UK party. Farage intends to make the reciprocal visit after he invited Jordan Bardella, Le Pen’s successor as RN leader, to his party conference in Birmingham on Friday. The pair joined each other on stage to sign a meter-high agreement to deport all migrants who cross the Channel illegally back to France, though the finer details are yet to be fleshed out. RN is due to hold its own party conference on Oct. 24-25 in Orléans, near Paris. The official quoted above, who was granted anonymity to discuss the plans, did not confirm whether Farage’s return visit would involve attending this conference. Advertisement Advertisement The official added that Farage plans a series of other visits to leaders on the European right before the end of 2026. Farage has had a long association with Marine Le Pen and interviewed her for his radio show in 2017. He said Friday that while he would not have struck a deal with the National Front founded by her father Jean-Marie Le Pen, her rechristened party had moved away from “extreme elements.” The relationship has not always been so harmonious. Farage said in 2024 that RN’s economic policies would be a “disaster” for France and “even worse for the economy than the current lot.” However, the two parties have forged closer links over their hard line on immigration issues. Le Pen is the favorite in the first round of voting in France’s 2027 presidential election, while POLITICO’s Poll of Polls now has Farage’s Reform UK one percentage point behind the ruling Labour Party ahead of the next general election, due by 2029. Farage alluded to a return visit from the conference stage in Birmingham after Bardella’s speech, which he gave in English — a rare move for him in public. Farage said: “The only downside is I think they’re going to invite me to go to Paris and I’ll have to speak in French, but never mind, we’ll get there.”

https://www.sciencealert.com/this-17th-c.text: This 17th-Century Aristocrat Had an Ingenious Secret For Keeping Her Teeth Health 29 August 2026 By Fiona MacDonald Add ScienceAlert on Google (Colleter et al., J. Archaeol. Sci. Rep. , 2023) In 1988, archaeologists cracked open a lead coffin inside the Château de Laval in northwestern France and found something peculiar. A woman who had been dead for more than 350 years, but whose teeth looked better than you would expect. She'd been embalmed, which helped. But something in her mouth caught the team's attention: a strange metal fixture wound around her teeth. Nobody in 1988 had the tools to work out what it actually was, or why it was there. So the mystery went back into storage, along with the coffin. It took another 35 years, a fresh set of dental scanners, and a very patient team of archaeologists to finally answer the question. The skeleton belonged to Anne d'Alègre, a French aristocrat who died in 1619 at the age of 54. And according to a 2023 study in the Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports , d'Alègre spent her final years quietly fighting to keep her own teeth in her head – using gold wire. (A) Location of Laval, France where the lead coffin (B) was discovered. Oil on canvas (C) representing the portrait of Anne d'Alègre after 1583. (Colleter et al., J. Archaeol. Sci. Rep. , 2023) A cone beam scan – a type of 3D X-ray – found that gold wiring had been threaded through several of d'Alègre's teeth, tightening and bracing them in place. She also had a false tooth carved from elephant ivory, not the hippopotamus ivory that was fashionable at the time. It wasn't just a cosmetic flourish. D'Alègre had severe periodontal (gum) disease , the kind that loosens teeth in their sockets until they fall out on their own. The gold wire was there to buy her time. "We propose that the objective of the treatment was triple: therapeutic, aesthetic, and societal," anthropologist Rozenn Colleter from INRAP, the French National Institute for Preventive Archaeological Research, and colleagues wrote in their journal article . Close-ups of the wire and prosthetics. Circled in D is what remains of wiring fixed to a tooth with considerable cervical wear (damage at the gum line). (Colleter et al., J. Archaeol. Sci. Rep. , 2023) Alas, d'Alègre's makeshift wiring probably didn't help – at least not directly. Wiring like this needs constant retightening, and every adjustment put more strain on the teeth next door – loosening those too. D'Alègre would have known that. She kept doing it anyway. At the time, a good set of teeth wasn't just about comfort. Losing your teeth didn't just change how you looked – it changed how people heard you. "If the patient remains toothless and disfigured, his speech becomes depraved," according to 16th-century physician to French kings, Ambroise Paré . A photograph (A) and cone-beam computed tomography scan (B) of d'Alègre's upper and lower jawbones. (Colleter et al., J. Archaeol. Sci. Rep. , 2023) For d'Alègre, that mattered more than most. She was a twice-widowed socialite – exactly the kind of woman whose face and voice were being judged, constantly, by a society that tied a woman's worth to how she presented herself. "Beyond the only aesthetic aspects, the installation of a dental prosthesis, and despite the possible odontological complications known at that time, perhaps allowed Anne d'Alègre to maintain a certain social rank in front of her detractors," Colleter and colleagues wrote . D'Alègre was a Huguenot – a French Protestant – who lived through the French Wars of Religion, fighting on the Protestant side against the Catholic crown. By 21, she was already a widow with a young son, Guy XX de Laval. When the Eighth War of Religion broke out, mother and son were forced into hiding as the king seized their land. Her son eventually converted to Catholicism, went off to fight in Hungary, and died in battle at 20. D'Alègre outlived him, married again, was widowed again, and died of illness at 54 – her teeth still wired into her jaw. But those teeth were weathered, worn down, possibly from d'Alègre grinding her teeth or clenching her jaw. "We have noted that the bruxism observed on Anne d'Alègre could be the sign of important stress states," the researchers wrote . "Her artificial teeth were probably not just a coquetry on her part. The various widowhoods she experienced undoubtedly contributed to her anxiety." Related: Hidden Crotch Detail Solves a 500-Year-Old Leonardo Da Vinci Mystery Today, severe periodontal disease affects an estimated 1 billion adults worldwide, according to the World Health Organization . Most of us just don't have gold wire and elephant ivory on hand to fight back, but we may soon have access to experimental treatments that can repair enamel and fight tooth decay – without drilling. The research has been published in the Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports . This article was fact-checked by Clare Watson and edited by Clare Watson . https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-says-musk-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OEgh Ukraine depends on Starlink for communications, logistics and drone operations Image: Andriy Andriyenko/Ukrainian Armed Forces/REUTERS Advertisement Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy 's office confirmed on Wednesday that the country's military has been cut off from full access to SpaceX's Starlink satellite system as it seeks to defend itself against a now nearly five-year Russian invasion. Russia launched an unprovoked, illegal, full-scale invasion of neighboring Ukraine on February 24, 2022 . "Tonight SpaceX introduced a speed limit for the Starlink terminals in motion," said Presidential Adviser Sergiy Beskrestnov. "Our defence forces were not warned about this restriction, which led to the disruption of a number of missions," he added. "Obviously, this action cannot be a coincidence and is linked to the current political situation," he added. Starlink cut-off coincides with Trump's 'energy ceasefire' That political situation refers to US President Donald Trump 's recent decision to lift sanctions on buying Russian oil. Trump has also criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy — saying he needs to stop attacking Russian oil infrastructure and that he should be replaced because "he won't make a deal" with Russia. Oil and gas prices have skyrocketed this year due to the US and Israel's war on Iran and its global consequences. Russia has meanwhile continued to target Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure as winter approaches. Trump has insisted, without providing evidence, that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an "energy ceasefire." But Moscow and Kyiv have both denied this. On Tuesday evening, Russian ballistic missiles hit a Kyiv power plant. Ukrainian officials said the Starlink outages had coincided with overnight Russian attacks. Will Elon Musk give Ukraine Starlink's eyes over Russia? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video SpaceX decision has impacted Ukraine's ability to defend itself Ukrainian troops use Starlink to conduct drone operations and internet terminals supplied by Elon Musk 's company are key to operating long-distance strikes. Presidential Advisor Beskrestnov said SpaceX had cut off access to its military-grade version of Starlink above 100 miles per hour (160 km/h), adding that Ukraine's 7th Rapid Reaction Corps, deployed in the southeast, had been forced to cancel some missions. "According to our ‌observations, during flights, the connection could drop for 10–20 seconds at speeds of ‌just 110–120 ​km/h. The drones kept moving, but these interruptions made them harder to control," a Reaction Corps representative told Reuters news agency. A source in Ukraine's Defense Ministry said such limitations significantly complicate logistics and ​drone operations. Ukraine has used Starlink terminals as an alternative to radio control for its drones as well as for ground communications since shortly after Russia launched its invasion. Starlink's resistance to electronic jamming has made it a crucial tool for flying long-range attack drones as well as large hexacopters that drop supplies for Ukraine's frontline troops. Elon Musk, the world's richest man and a key Donald Trump supporter, has, however, repeatedly shifted his stance on Ukraine since the early days of Russia's invasion. In August, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said Kyiv was looking to create an alternative to Musk's Starlink, in concert "with a European country."
